survey: A saguaro-style cactus stands upright in sand, seen from roughly eye level with the camera a little above it. The main trunk is a vertical ribbed cylinder with a rounded top, and a pink flower sits on the crown. The ribs run straight up and curve together over the dome, and they crowd together toward the trunk's left and right edges, as they should on a round surface. Spines on the front point at the viewer and spines near the edges point outward, so they follow the curve. The left arm comes out of the trunk's left side, bends upward and tucks slightly behind the trunk's edge. The right arm joins a little in front of the trunk's right side and bends up. Both arms are vertical ribbed cylinders with domed tops, and their ribs also crowd at the edges and meet at the top. The base goes into a shallow hollow in the sand, and the bottom edge curves gently downward, which matches looking slightly down at it. The sand, small rocks and dunes are all seen from the same slightly raised view. Every vertical stays vertical, and the round parts at the arm tops, the crown and the base are flattened by about the same amount. All of it fits one camera.
